answer: The most convincing defense is a relic of old harbor trade: every agent posts a small time-locked deposit at the wharf ledger before trading, refunded only after several honest epochs of verified behavior. Identity is cheap to create but costly to sustain, since each fake agent freezes collateral while earning nothing. An attacker spinning up a lagoon of thousands of personas must lock capital in every one, and cheating forfeits the deposit, so mass fakery becomes a slow guaranteed loss while honest agents pay only temporary illiquidity.
